idiom_name: enum with a variant per rule + match in eval, Box for recursive children
implementation_notes: The canonical Rust realization: one enum with a variant per grammar rule, children behind Box (or Rc/Arc to share subtrees) because recursive types need indirection, and evaluation a match the compiler checks for exhaustiveness - adding a variant breaks every evaluator until it is handled. Failures travel in Result, so evaluation has no exceptions and the caller decides how to report a bad expression.
pitfalls: Box per child means one heap allocation per node; wide trees are usually better served by a Vec-backed arena with indices, or Rc when subtrees are shared.
Plain + wraps on overflow in release builds: use checked_add or enable overflow-checks for an interpreter that must be correct.

match on &Expr yields references, so small Copy payloads need dereferencing and larger ones need clone() or borrowing accessors - forgetting this produces borrow-checker puzzles, not bugs, but costs time.

variants.name: Trait objects with Box<dyn Expr> children
variants.idiom_name: trait Expr declaring eval + one struct per rule, children as Box<dyn Expr>
variants.implementation_notes: The object-oriented realization Rust still supports: a trait declaring the evaluate operation, one struct per grammar rule, and children as Box<dyn Expr>. Dynamic dispatch is what you want when the node set must stay open to other crates (grammar plugins, user-supplied node types) or when heterogeneous nodes are stored behind one type; the price is a vtable call per node, no exhaustiveness checking, and downcasting when the node kind must be recovered.
pitfalls: Trait objects require a dyn-compatible trait: generic methods or Self-returning methods make the trait unusable behind dyn.
Adding an operation means editing the trait and every implementor - the mirror image of adding a variant to an enum, and the reason to choose one shape deliberately.
Downcasting via Any is possible but is a design smell: if the evaluator must recover concrete node kinds, the enum form was probably right.
